title: The Surprising Reason You Prefer Familiar Things
hook: Why do you like songs more after hearing them repeatedly?

narration.text: Your brain often prefers things you have encountered before.
This is called the mere exposure effect in psychology.
Repeated exposure makes something feel safer and less threatening.
Our brains process familiar stimuli more easily.
This ease of processing registers as a feeling of liking.
It happens even when you are not consciously aware of the repeated exposure.
So, advertisers use this effect to make products seem more appealing.
Have you noticed yourself liking something more after seeing it everywhere?

description: Discover the psychological phenomenon that makes us prefer things we have seen or heard many times. Learn why familiarity can breed affection and how it influences your daily choices, often without you even realising it.
topic: Why familiarity makes us prefer certain things, explaining the mere exposure effect in psychology.
